title: Push a slide's ball retainer to its front stop, then roll the inner member in between its rollers until it seats
instruction: Push the orange ball retainer inside the grey slide channel toward the channel's open end until it stops. Then pick up the blue inner member, slide its tapered end into the channel's open end level and square, and push it in until it stops against the block near the far end.
context: Lenovo ThinkSystem SR850 V4, Install the server to the rack: "Ensure that the ball retainer is at the foremost of the intermediate rail before inserting the inner rail into the intermediate rail." https://pubs.lenovo.com/sr850-v4/install_the_server_to_rail Accuride 3832CDO data sheet, step 4: "Make sure the ball bearing retainers in the cabinet side are fully forward." https://static.datasheets.com/doc/6720634-accuride-3832-c26-do-ds.pdf The cost otherwise, Accuride patent US 8,500,223 B2: "if the bearing retainer is not maintained in such a position then misalignment of the inner slide member with respect to the outer slide member during the reinsertion process may result in inadvertent contact between the inner slide member and the bearing retainer", which "may well result in damage to the bearing retainer." https://patents.google.com/patent/US8500223B2/en The balls roll, so the retainer moves half as far as the inner member; left 90 mm back, it meets the member 90 mm early; in our wrong-order runs the member stalled 45 to 94 mm short of home. Done by: data-center technicians racking servers; installers fitting drawer and equipment slides.
setup: Table coordinates: x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; arm bases at y = +0.305 and -0.305. A grey steel slide channel (the intermediate member) lies on the table, open side up, fixed, its centre line along y at x = 0.32 from its closed back end at y = -0.17 to its open end at y = +0.08 (250 mm). Inside 32 mm wide; walls 2 mm thick and 21.5 mm tall; lips 1.5 mm thick at the top leave a 26 mm opening. A 10 mm guide shelf 4.5 mm tall lines the open end, a stop block fills the channel 22 to 30 mm from the back end, and a bracket 10 x 36 x 23 mm closes the back. The orange ball retainer rides in the channel on a slide joint: a cage 93.5 x 29 mm (4 bars, 17 to 20.5 mm above the table) carrying three stations of two 5 mm steel rollers, a lower one on the floor and a sprung upper one that hangs 1 mm into the inner member's path. It starts with its back end 63.5 mm from the channel's back end, 90 mm short of its front stop, and slides against about 7 N of drag. The blue aluminium inner member, 250 x 30 x 8 mm, 150 g, its last 30 mm tapered to 25 x 3 mm, lies flat on the table centred at (0.22, 0.20), tapered end toward -y.
scoring: Riding position: the inner member's centre within 1.5 mm of the channel's centre line and of riding height (11 mm above the table), within 1.5 degrees of the channel's line both flat and nose up or down. Meeting the retainer: either end inside the channel's cavity (between the walls, under the lips, between the back end and the mouth, the member within 15 degrees of the channel's line) and no more than 2 mm ahead of the cage's front bar (9.5 mm ahead of the front rollers; a member carried 4.5 mm or more high strikes it first). Each time an end first meets the retainer, the retainer must be within 15 mm of its front stop; while the end stays there, the retainer may not fall more than 5 mm behind where rolling from its position at that first meeting would leave it (a shove trips this after 5 mm at the bar, 10 mm at the rollers). A miss scores 0 for the rest of the trial, however the member ends up. Home: the tapered end within 2 mm of the stop block. 1.0 when home in riding position, having met the retainer forward, with the member and the retainer still (under 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s, which ends the trial. At the last step: 0.9 for the same state; 0.75 if home but moving; 0.3 to 0.7 by depth between the front rollers and home when in riding position and having met the retainer forward; 0.2 when the retainer is within 15 mm of its front stop or the member met it forward; 0 otherwise. The scorer sees poses and speeds, not the grippers. On a real rig the order needs video; a wrong order also leaves the member sticking out 75 to 125 mm instead of 30 mm.
reset_notes: Pull the inner member out, lay it flat on its start mark, and slide the retainer back 90 mm from its front stop.
fidelity: Approximate: the channel is fixed boxes, open side up; no outer member. Each ball pair is one 5 mm roller on a free hinge, three stations; upper rollers sprung down about 40 N so a stalled pair skids only above about 48 N, stiffer than a real slide. Retainer drag is a pad on the floor. Stop block 30 mm short of flush so a gripper can push the end. Section, mass (aluminium), ball size and retainer travel are estimates; length is the 3832-C10's. Friction 1.2/1.0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps; scored before two order-memory changes, same scene and meshes; the member never enters the channel, so neither change can raise it); demo: 1.0 (success at step 709)
